prompt_text: Where should I stay in Branson Missouri, an Airbnb or a hotel, and which specific places are best?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: It depends on what you want from the trip.

- Stay in a hotel (on or near 76 “The Strip” / downtown) if you want convenience for shows, restaurants, predictable service, pools/breakfast and easy last-minute bookings.  
- Stay in an Airbnb/cabin if you want more space, a kitchen, privacy or a lakeside/woods experience — especially good for families, groups, or a quieter/table-rock-lake getaway.  
- For a splurge or a true resort experience choose a lakeside resort/cabin property.

Recommended options by type

1) Hotels for convenience / shows (best if you’ll be on the 76 Country Boulevard Strip)
- Hilton Branson Convention Center — centrally located for shows and the Convention Center; dependable amenities.  
- Grand Country Inn (or similar family-oriented hotels on 76) — budget-friendly, family-focused, right on the Strip so evening shows are easy to reach.  
- Staybridge Suites / other extended-stay hotels downtown or near Branson Landing — good if you want a kitchen plus hotel services.

2) Upscale lakeside / resort stays (romantic or luxury/outdoor activities)
- Chateau on the Lake Resort, Spa & Convention Center — lakefront, spa, nice views and higher-end amenities.  
- Big Cedar Lodge (nearby, Ridgedale/Indian Point area) — high-end cabins and resort amenities, excellent if you want outdoor recreation and a destination resort vibe.

3) Unique / local stay experiences
- The Keeter Center at the College of the Ozarks — a well-regarded inn/restaurant experience unique to the area (if you’re interested in a different, high-quality local option).  
- Themed or boutique hotels on and near the Strip — good if you want convenience with a bit of local character.

4) Cabins/Airbnbs (best for groups, families, privacy, lake access)
- Lakefront cabins on Table Rock Lake (Indian Point, Kimberling City area) — great for boating, privacy and large groups; often cheaper per person and include kitchen/grill.  
- Cabins closer to Silver Dollar City — if you plan to spend most time at the theme park, staying nearby saves driving.

How to choose (quick checklist)
- Trip purpose: shows/strip = hotel; lake/cabins/outdoors = Airbnb/cabin/resort.  
- Group size: large groups = Airbnb/cabin or condo; couples or solo = hotel or boutique inn.  
- Amenities: need breakfast/pool/front desk? pick a hotel. Need kitchen/private dock? pick a rental.  
- Convenience vs. experience: hotels = convenience; rentals = experience.  
- Booking tips: read recent reviews, confirm parking access, check cancellation rules and cleaning fees, and verify short-term rental legality (Branson-area rules can change).

Practical location tips
- 76 Country Boulevard (“the Strip”) — best for show-hopping and tourist attractions.  
- Branson Landing / downtown — lakefront dining and shopping, good midtown location.  
- Indian Point / Table Rock Lake / Kimberling City / Big Cedar area — best for lake cabins and quiet outdoor time.  
- Near Silver Dollar City (Hwy 76 west) — best if the theme park is your main activity.

If you tell me: dates, how many people, budget, and whether you prefer shows or lake time, I can recommend 3–5 specific hotels or Airbnb-style listings with links and price guidance.
